subject: XpressPay discovery recap — model snapshot, stability options, and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@xpresspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: XpressPay discovery recap + suggested immediate next steps

Thanks again for taking time today, Sanjay — good conversation and helpful context on fraud-flagging latency tolerances and the 24/7 transaction window. Quick recap and suggested path forward: 

- Primary business need: reduce false positives on card-not-present transactions while keeping end-to-end decision latency under 200ms for baseline flows.
- Data: you confirmed access to a 3-month sample of labeled decisions + the streaming request schema.
- Success criteria: precision lift >= 6% at same recall, P95 latency < 250ms in staging, clear rollback path for model changes.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) We’ll run a 1-week fit evaluation using: rw-compact-7b-chat (latency-focused) and rw-super-13b (higher quality, quantized) against your prompt set.
2) Please drop the sample dataset and the initial prompt files into the Drive folder linked below. We attached an initial prompt CSV with the formats we expect.
3) Marissa will share a benchmark plan and an evaluation packet (prompts, automated metrics, and a diff checklist).
4) If results look good, we recommend a canary rollout pinned to the evaluated model snapshot with a 24–48 hour watch window and automatic fallback to the current variant on drift above threshold.

Attachments: xpresspay_poc_prompts.csv (sample prompts), benchmark-summary-20270111.pdf (template).
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bxp-XpressPay-eval

Happy to hop back on a short follow-up if you want to walk the plan. Next step from our side: run the eval and present a 1-page ops guardrail + rollback matrix by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@xpresspay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: XpressPay discovery recap + suggested immediate next steps

Thanks Priyom — this looks exactly like what we discussed. A couple quick clarifying asks before you run the eval: 

- Regression risk: last time we saw a model upgrade it increased false negatives by ~3 points in one of our edge flows. Can you include a diffs summary that highlights changes in top-negative classes and a suggested pin/rollback trigger?
- Pinning: our security team prefers a hard pin for 48 hours for production changes. Can you propose a pin-and-monitor approach that integrates with our incident runbook?

We’ll upload the sample dataset today. Also adding procurement on this thread to start the paperwork once we have a recommended path.

—Sanjay
Director, Risk Ops — XpressPay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@xpresspay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: XpressPay discovery recap + suggested immediate next steps

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the callout. Below is the concrete eval plan and the version-stability playbook we’ll execute. I’ve attached the benchmark summary and a draft mutual action plan.

Evaluation plan (1 week, staging):
- Models to test: rw-compact-7b-chat (primary latency candidate), rw-super-13b-quant (primary quality candidate).
- Test sets: 3k randomly sampled historical transactions + 600 edge-case prompts from your team (we’ll keep these sealed for regression checks).
- Metrics: precision@decision-threshold, false_negative_rate_by_segment (card-present / card-not-present / cross-border), P50/P95 latency.
- Deliverables: per-model confusion matrices, token-latency distributions, and a diffs artifact that lists top 20 example prompts with divergent outputs between baseline and candidate.

Version-stability / rollback playbook (summary):
1) Snapshot + artifacting: every evaluated candidate will be saved as a snapshot id (e.g., rw-super-13b-quant:snap-20270112-001). We’ll archive the exact prompt set and any prompt-engineering layers used.
2) Canary & pin strategy: deploy candidate to 2% of traffic for 6 hours. If key metrics (precision lift, false_negative_rate_by_segment, P95 latency) remain within pre-agreed bounds, we escalate to 25% for 24 hours. At 25% we require no increase in false negatives > 1.0 point and P95 latency < 300ms.
3) Hard pin option: you can request a 48-hour hard pin where the candidate is fixed for 48h and automatic model upgrades are disabled. Request is applied via the Console UI and emits an audit event.
4) Automatic rollback triggers: any time false negatives increase by >1.5 absolute points for the monitored segments OR P95 latency degrades >20% relative to baseline, the system will automatically route traffic back to the pinned baseline and create an incident with our SRE/CS on-call.
5) Diff artifact and human review: after a canary we’ll produce a prioritized diff list (examples + model outputs) and highlight any cases likely to impact user experience; that will feed a short QA session with your team before full rollout.

Additional notes:
- We will produce a short PromptSet CSV (attached) that maps transaction types to canonical prompts; this is the minimal surface we will use for regression checks.
- For transparency, we’ll include the eval notebook and the raw result tables in the Drive folder so your engineers can replay any case.

Attachments: benchmark-summary-20270111.pdf, xpresspay_poc_prompts.csv, mutual-action-plan-XP-4127.docx
Links: https://app.redwood.com/evals/XP-4127/summary

If that looks good, Priyom — can we schedule a 30-minute sync with Sanjay + procurement tomorrow afternoon to confirm the canary thresholds and the hard pin language in the MSA?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, XpressPay Procurement <procurement@xpresspay.com>

Subject: Re: XpressPay discovery recap — model snapshot, stability options, and next steps

Perfect — thanks Sanjay and Marissa. Action items and owners: 

- XpressPay: upload sample dataset + edge-case prompts to Drive (Sanjay) — target: EOD today.
- Redwood (Marissa): kick off eval run as soon as samples are available; share raw results and the diff artifact within 24 hours of complete data.
- Redwood (Priyom): schedule a 30-minute threshold review with XpressPay + procurement for tomorrow 1/13 11:00am PT; prepare the MSA clause language for a 48-hour hard pin and automatic rollback triggers.
- Procurement: review mutual-action-plan-XP-4127.docx and confirm procurement contact for contracting.

We’ve added a DocuSign preview to the Drive folder for the MAP; procurement feel free to start redlines in the document. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bxp-XpressPay-eval

If there’s anything urgent, ping me directly. Looking forward to running the fit checks and getting a safe canary in place.

Best,
Priyom
